title: Gauging the interplay between market liquidity and funding liquidity
summary: This ECB Financial Stability Review special feature examines the relationship between market liquidity and funding liquidity in the euro area. The paper constructs composite indicators for both liquidity dimensions and analyzes how they interact to potentially generate liquidity spirals. The authors identify structural factors (market-making practices, issue size, trade transparency, investor landscape) and cyclical determinants (risk appetite, macroeconomic conditions, monetary policy cycles) that affect liquidity conditions.
key_points: Market liquidity is defined as the ability to rapidly execute large securities transactions at low cost with limited price impact, with dimensions including immediacy, breadth/depth, tightness, and resilience
Funding liquidity encompasses the ease of obtaining deposits and borrowing conditions, with risk types including rollover risk, redemption risk, and haircut/margining risk
Market liquidity and funding liquidity are inherently connected and can reinforce each other, generating adverse liquidity spirals with potential for systemic stress

Structural drivers of liquidity include market-making practices, issue size, trade transparency, and investor landscape; cyclical drivers include investor risk appetite, macro conditions, and monetary policy cycles
The paper notes data quality challenges including sparse corporate bond trading data due to OTC fragmentation, lack of consolidated tape providers, and gaps in non-bank financial intermediary data
Cyclical factors are identified as turning more restrictive as policy normalizes, raising concerns about a shift to less system liquidity and more fragile conditions
why_it_matters: Understanding the interplay between market and funding liquidity is critical for financial stability risk management. When market liquidity evaporates, financial market pricing becomes less reliable and tends to overreact, leading to increased volatility and higher funding costs. Funding liquidity enables market participants to absorb demand/supply fluctuations. Under extreme conditions, markets can stop functioning altogether. This analysis helps policymakers, regulators, and market participants identify vulnerabilities before liquidity spirals emerge.
macro_context: The analysis situates liquidity concerns within the broader context of high financial market volatility, increased recession risk, bouts of heightened risk aversion, and monetary policy normalization. The authors note that a constellation of subdued free float of high-quality debt securities and globally high inflation has increased bond market volatility and uncertainty about the future path of monetary policy.
market_structure_context: The paper provides detailed market structure analysis including: dimensions of market liquidity (immediacy, breadth/depth, tightness, resilience of market-makers), funding liquidity risk categories, and the interaction mechanisms between market and funding liquidity. It also highlights structural data gaps including fragmented OTC bond trading, lack of consolidated tape providers, and limited visibility into algorithmic trading and principal trading firm activities.
